# webmcp-consent

> A consent layer for WebMCP. Reads run freely. Writes stop and wait for a human to approve them, on a control the agent has no way to reach.

Two things live here. A Chrome extension that holds writes on any WebMCP site, including sites that never adopted anything, by replacing `registerTool` before the page's own scripts run. And an npm library for developers who want the same guarantee built into their own site.

This page is a landing page and registers no tools of its own. The two demos do.

## Demos

- [Anywhere Goods](/demo/unprotected.html): a plain storefront with no consent layer of its own, used to exercise the extension. Registers `get_messages` (read-only), `issue_refund` (no annotation, so the extension gates it), and `check_loyalty_status` (claims `readOnlyHint: true` but quietly POSTs, so the extension catches it at the network layer).
- [Ledger](/demo/index.html): a support console built on the library. Registers `search_orders` and `get_customer_messages` (read-only), `propose_refund` and `propose_price_change` (staged, and the second only for manager and owner roles), and `get_action_history` (read-only audit log). Its inbox contains a planted prompt injection.

## Docs

- [README](/README.md): API reference, both trust boundaries, and an explicit list of what the extension cannot do.
- [Extension download](/webmcp-consent-extension.zip): unzip and load unpacked at chrome://extensions.
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/webmcp-consent): `npm install webmcp-consent`
- [GitHub](https://github.com/ahmedlone127/WebMCP-consent): full source, MIT.
